mutations)**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nServer Actions (functions with &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use server\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;) are exposed as public endpoints, just like API routes. Always verify authentication and authorization **inside** each Server Action—do not rely solely on middleware, layout guards, or page-level checks, as Server Actions can be invoked directly.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nNext.js documentation explicitly states: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Treat Server Actions with the same security considerations as public-facing API endpoints, and verify if the user is allowed to perform a mutation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Incorrect (no authentication check):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function deleteUser(userId: string) {\\\\\\\\n  // Anyone can call this! session.user.id !== userId) {\\\\\\\\n    throw unauthorized('Cannot delete other users')\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  await db.user.delete({ where: { id: userId } })\\\\\\\\n  return { success: true }\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**With input validation:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\\\\\\\\n'use server'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nimport { verifySession } from '@/lib/auth'\\\\\\\\nimport { z } from 'zod'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nconst updateProfileSchema = z.object({\\\\\\\\n  userId: z.string().uuid(),\\\\\\\\n  name: z.string().min(1).max(100),\\\\\\\\n  email: z.string().email()\\\\\\\\n})\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function updateProfile(data: unknown) {\\\\\\\\n  // Validate input first\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"title: Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"impact: CRITICAL\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"impactDescription: prevents unauthorized access to server mutations\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"tags: server, server-actions, authentication, security, authorization\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":5},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":6},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":7},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"## Authenticate Server Actions Like API Routes\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":9},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"**Impact: CRITICAL (prevents unauthorized access to server mutations)**\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":10},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":11},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Server Actions (functions with &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use server\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;) are exposed as public endpoints, just like API routes. {\\\\\\\\n    const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown'\\\\\\\\n    const sessionCookie = (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous'\\\\\\\\n    \\\\\\\\n    logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent })\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), {\\\\\\\\n    status: 200,\\\\\\\\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe response is sent immediately while logging happens in the background.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Common use cases:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Analytics tracking\\\\\\\\n- Audit logging\\\\\\\\n- Sending notifications\\\\\\\\n- Cache invalidation\\\\\\\\n- Cleanup tasks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Important notes:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;after()&#96; How to create forms with Server Actions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## How it works\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact extends the HTML [&#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [&#96;action&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen used in a form, the function automatically receives the [&#96;FormData&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [&#96;FormData&#96; methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [&#96;Object.fromEntries()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: &#96;const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)&#96;. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with &#96;$ACTION_&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Passing additional arguments\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOutside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [&#96;bind&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. For example, to pass the &#96;userId&#96; argument to the &#96;updateUser&#96; Server Function:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx If you are not using React 19, only the &#96;pending&#96; key is available.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Optimistic updates\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can use the React [&#96;useOptimistic&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic) hook to optimistically update the UI before the Server Function finishes executing, rather than waiting for the response:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ntype Message = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  message: string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }: { messages: Message[] }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = useOptimistic&lt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    Message[],\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  &gt;(messages, (state, newMessage) =&gt; [...state, { message: newMessage }])\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const formAction = async (formData: FormData) =&gt; {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const message = formData.get('message') as string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {optimisticMessages.map((m, i) =&gt; (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;div key={i}&gt;{m.message}&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      ))}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"message\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;button type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = useOptimistic(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    messages,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    (state, newMessage) =&gt; [...state, { message: newMessage }]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const formAction = async (formData) =&gt; {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const message = formData.get('message')\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {optimisticMessages.map((m) =&gt; (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;div&gt;{m.message}&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      ))}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"message\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;button type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Nested form elements\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can call Server Actions in elements nested inside &#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96; such as &#96;&lt;button&gt;&#96;, &#96;&lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;&#96;, and &#96;&lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"image\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;&#96;. These elements accept the &#96;formAction&#96; prop or event handlers.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis is useful in cases where you want to call multiple Server Actions within a form. For example, you can create a specific &#96;&lt;button&gt;&#96; element for saving a post draft in addition to publishing it. See the [React &#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96; docs](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/form#handling-multiple-submission-types) for more information.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Programmatic form submission\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can trigger a form submission programmatically using the [&#96;requestSubmit()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLFormElement/requestSubmit) method. For example, when the user submits a form using the &#96;⌘&#96; + &#96;Enter&#96; keyboard shortcut, you can listen for the &#96;onKeyDown&#96; e.preventDefault()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      e.currentTarget.form?.requestSubmit()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx How to create forms with Server Actions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## How it works\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact extends the HTML [&#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [&#96;action&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen used in a form, the function automatically receives the [&#96;FormData&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [&#96;FormData&#96; methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [&#96;Object.fromEntries()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: &#96;const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)&#96;. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with &#96;$ACTION_&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Passing additional arguments\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOutside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [&#96;bind&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. For example, to pass the &#96;userId&#96; argument to the &#96;updateUser&#96; Server Function:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/client-component.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { updateUser } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function UserProfile({ userId }: { userId: string }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const updateUserWithId = updateUser.bind(null, userId)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;form action={updateUserWithId}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;input However, the value will be part of the rendered HTML and will not be encoded.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; * &#96;bind&#96; works in both Server and Client Components and supports progressive enhancement.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Form validation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nForms can be validated on the client or server.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **client-side validation**, you can use the HTML attributes like &#96;required&#96; and &#96;type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"email\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; for basic validation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **server-side validation**, you can use a library like [zod](https://zod.dev/) to validate the form fields. For example:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/actions.ts\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use pending] = useActionState(createUser, initialState)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements initialState)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;button disabled={pending}&gt;Sign up&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nAlternatively, you can use the [&#96;useFormStatus&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/hooks/useFormStatus) hook to show a loading indicator while the action is being executed. When using this hook, you'll need to create a separate component to render the loading indicator. For example, to disable the button when the action is pending:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;button disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;button disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can then nest the &#96;SubmitButton&#96; component inside the form:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;form action={createUser}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;SubmitButton /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;form action={createUser}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;SubmitButton /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; **Good to know:** In React 19, &#96;useFormStatus&#96; includes additional keys on the returned object, like data, method, and action. If you are not using React 19, only the &#96;pending&#96; key is available.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Optimistic updates\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can use the React [&#96;useOptimistic&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic) hook to optimistically update the UI before the Server Function finishes executing, rather than waiting for the response:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ntype Message = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  message: string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }: { messages: Message[] }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = useOptimistic&lt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    Message[],\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  &gt;(messages, (state, newMessage) =&gt; [...state, { message: newMessage }])\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const formAction = async (formData: FormData) =&gt; {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const message = formData.get('message') as string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {optimisticMessages.map((m, i) =&gt; (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;div key={i}&gt;{m.message}&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      ))}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"message\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;button type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = useOptimistic(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    messages,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    (state, newMessage) =&gt; [...state, { message: newMessage }]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const formAction = async (formData) =&gt; {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const message = formData.get('message')\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {optimisticMessages.map((m) =&gt; (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;div&gt;{m.message}&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      ))}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"message\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;button type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Nested form elements\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can call Server Actions in elements nested inside &#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96; such as &#96;&lt;button&gt;&#96;, &#96;&lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;&#96;, and &#96;&lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"image\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;&#96;. These elements accept the &#96;formAction&#96; prop or event handlers.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis is useful in cases where you want to call multiple Server Actions within a form. For example, you can create a specific &#96;&lt;button&gt;&#96; element for saving a post draft in addition to publishing it. VALIDATE — parse and validate all inputs with Zod\\\\\\\\n  const rawData = {\\\\\\\\n    title: formData.get(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"title\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"),\\\\\\\\n    description: formData.get(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"description\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"),\\\\\\\\n    url: formData.get(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"url\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\") || \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n    repoUrl: formData.get(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"repoUrl\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\") || \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\\n    status: formData.get(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"status\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"),\\\\\\\\n  };\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  const validatedData = CreateProjectSchema.parse(rawData);\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // 3. EXECUTE — use Drizzle ORM (parameterized queries, no string concatenation)\\\\\\\\n  await db.insert(projects).values({\\\\\\\\n    title: validatedData.title,\\\\\\\\n    description: validatedData.description,\\\\\\\\n    url: validatedData.url || undefined,\\\\\\\\n    repoUrl: validatedData.repoUrl || undefined,\\\\\\\\n    status: validatedData.status,\\\\\\\\n    order: 0,\\\\\\\\n  });\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n  // 4. This prevents logging, analytics, and other side effects from blocking the response.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Incorrect (blocks response):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\\\\\\\\n  // Perform mutation\\\\\\\\n  await updateDatabase(request)\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Logging blocks the response\\\\\\\\n  const userAgent = request.headers.get('user-agent') || 'unknown'\\\\\\\\n  await logUserAction({ userAgent })\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), {\\\\\\\\n    status: 200,\\\\\\\\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Correct (non-blocking):**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx\\\\\\\\nimport { after } from 'next/server'\\\\\\\\nimport { headers, cookies } from 'next/headers'\\\\\\\\nimport { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils'\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\\\\\\\\n  // Perform mutation\\\\\\\\n  await updateDatabase(request)\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  // Log after response is sent\\\\\\\\n  after(async () =&gt; {\\\\\\\\n    const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown'\\\\\\\\n    const sessionCookie = (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous'\\\\\\\\n    \\\\\\\\n    logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent })\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n  \\\\\\\\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), {\\\\\\\\n    status: 200,\\\\\\\\n    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }\\\\\\\\n  })\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe response is sent immediately while logging happens in the background.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Common use cases:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Analytics tracking\\\\\\\\n- Audit logging\\\\\\\\n- Sending notifications\\\\\\\\n- Cache invalidation\\\\\\\\n- Cleanup tasks\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Important notes:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- &#96;after()&#96; runs even if the response fails or redirects\\\\\\\\n- Works in Server Actions, Route Handlers, and Server Components\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nReference: [https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after)\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"title: Use after() for Non-Blocking Operations\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"impact: MEDIUM\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"impactDescription: faster response times\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"tags: server, async, logging, analytics, side-effects\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":5},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":6},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":7},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"## Use after() for Non-Blocking Operations\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":9},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Use Next.js's &#96;after()&#96; How to create forms with Server Actions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## How it works\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact extends the HTML [&#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [&#96;action&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen used in a form, the function automatically receives the [&#96;FormData&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [&#96;FormData&#96; methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [&#96;Object.fromEntries()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: &#96;const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)&#96;. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with &#96;$ACTION_&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Passing additional arguments\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOutside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [&#96;bind&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. For example, to pass the &#96;userId&#96; argument to the &#96;updateUser&#96; Server Function:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx However, the value will be part of the rendered HTML and will not be encoded.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; * &#96;bind&#96; works in both Server and Client Components and supports progressive enhancement.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Form validation\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nForms can be validated on the client or server.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **client-side validation**, you can use the HTML attributes like &#96;required&#96; and &#96;type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"email\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; for basic validation.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n* For **server-side validation**, you can use a library like [zod](https://zod.dev/) to validate the form fields. can use the [&#96;useFormStatus&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/hooks/useFormStatus) hook to show a loading indicator while the action is being executed. For example, to disable the button when the action is pending:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;button disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/button.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" highlight={6} switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useFormStatus } from 'react-dom'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function SubmitButton() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const { pending } = useFormStatus()\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;button disabled={pending} type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      Sign Up\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can then nest the &#96;SubmitButton&#96; component inside the form:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;form action={createUser}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;SubmitButton /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/ui/signup.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { SubmitButton } from './button'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { createUser } from '@/app/actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Signup() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;form action={createUser}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {/* Other form elements */}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;SubmitButton /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; **Good to know:** In React 19, &#96;useFormStatus&#96; includes additional keys on the returned object, like data, method, and action. If you are not using React 19, only the &#96;pending&#96; key is available.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Optimistic updates\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can use the React [&#96;useOptimistic&#96;](https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic) hook to optimistically update the UI before the Server Function finishes executing, rather than waiting for the response:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ntype Message = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  message: string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }: { messages: Message[] }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = useOptimistic&lt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    Message[],\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  &gt;(messages, (state, newMessage) =&gt; [...state, { message: newMessage }])\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const formAction = async (formData: FormData) =&gt; {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const message = formData.get('message') as string\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {optimisticMessages.map((m, i) =&gt; (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;div key={i}&gt;{m.message}&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      ))}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"message\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;button type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n'use client'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { useOptimistic } from 'react'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nimport { send } from './actions'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport function Thread({ messages }) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const [optimisticMessages, addOptimisticMessage] = useOptimistic(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    messages,\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    (state, newMessage) =&gt; [...state, { message: newMessage }]\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  const formAction = async (formData) =&gt; {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const message = formData.get('message')\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    addOptimisticMessage(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    await send(message)\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      {optimisticMessages.map((m) =&gt; (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;div&gt;{m.message}&lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      ))}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;form action={formAction}&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" name=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"message\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" /&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n        &lt;button type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;Send&lt;/button&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      &lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    &lt;/div&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  )\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Nested form elements\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can call Server Actions in elements nested inside &#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96; such as &#96;&lt;button&gt;&#96;, &#96;&lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"submit\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;&#96;, and &#96;&lt;input type=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"image\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&gt;&#96;. These elements accept the &#96;formAction&#96; prop or event handlers.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nThis is useful in cases where you want to call multiple Server Actions within a form. For example, you can create a specific &#96;&lt;button&gt;&#96; element for saving a post draft in addition to publishing it. See the [React &#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96; docs](https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/components/form#handling-multiple-submission-types) for more information.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Programmatic form submission\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nYou can trigger a form submission programmatically using the [&#96;requestSubmit()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLFormElement/requestSubmit) method. For example, when the user submits a form using the &#96;⌘&#96; + &#96;Enter&#96; keyboard shortcut, you can listen for the &#96;onKeyDown&#96; How to create forms with Server Actions\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n@doc-version: 16.0.5\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact Server Actions are [Server Functions](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-functions) that execute on the server. They can be called in Server and Client Components to handle form submissions. This guide will walk you through how to create forms in Next.js with Server Actions.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## How it works\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nReact extends the HTML [&#96;&lt;form&gt;&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/form) element to allow Server Actions to be invoked with the [&#96;action&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/form#action) attribute.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nWhen used in a form, the function automatically receives the [&#96;FormData&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/FormData/FormData) object. You can then extract the data using the native [&#96;FormData&#96; methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/FormData#instance_methods):\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.tsx\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData: FormData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;jsx filename=\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"app/invoices/page.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" switcher\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nexport default function Page() {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  async function createInvoice(formData) {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    'use server'\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    const rawFormData = {\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      customerId: formData.get('customerId'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      amount: formData.get('amount'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n      status: formData.get('status'),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // mutate data\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n    // revalidate the cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n  return &lt;form action={createInvoice}&gt;...&lt;/form&gt;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&gt; **Good to know:** When working with forms that have multiple fields, use JavaScript's [&#96;Object.fromEntries()&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Object/fromEntries). For example: &#96;const rawFormData = Object.fromEntries(formData)&#96;. Note that this object will contain extra properties prefixed with &#96;$ACTION_&#96;.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n## Passing additional arguments\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nOutside of form fields, you can pass additional arguments to a Server Function using the JavaScript [&#96;bind&#96;](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Function/bind) method. For example, to pass the &#96;userId&#96; argument to the &#96;updateUser&#96; Server Function:\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n&#96;&#96;&#96;tsx Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast &gt;= AA.Technical constraints &amp; stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout &amp; sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta &amp; SEO   - Proper &#96;&lt;head&gt;&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact &amp; social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system &amp; visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing &amp; grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance &amp; best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). Import Tailwind in your CSS with &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;, not &#96;@tailwind&#96; directives.- Define design tokens, custom utilities, and settings in CSS using the new &#96;@theme&#96; at-rule and related directives (so there is no default &#96;tailwind.config.ts&#96;). If you intentionally want to keep a legacy JS/TS configuration, load it explicitly from CSS using &#96;@config \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"./tailwind.config.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (this is allowed for backward compatibility), but prefer CSS-first. - Use &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; for PostCSS setups or &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; when using Vite/Next dev tooling. Use &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; for CLI commands. - Keep compatibility with Tailwind v4 features: automatic content detection, CSS theme variables, container queries, and prefers-reduced-motion handling.Deliverables (explicit)- Output a complete project scaffold (files and code) ready to run with &#96;pnpm&#96;/&#96;npm&#96;:  - &#96;app/page.tsx&#96; (home)  - &#96;app/layout.tsx&#96; (meta, fonts, theme provider)  - &#96;components/*&#96; for each UI piece  - &#96;lib/data.ts&#96; or &#96;data/seed.ts&#96; with typed placeholder data  - &#96;public/&#96; with placeholder images (profile SVG) and &#96;resume.pdf&#96;  - &#96;styles/globals.css&#96; containing &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\";&#96; and your &#96;@theme&#96; declarations  - &#96;postcss.config.mjs&#96; referencing &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; if using PostCSS, or instructions to use &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; for Vite users  - &#96;package.json&#96; with &#96;tailwindcss&#96; v4 and &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; as appropriate- Include a small README with run instructions and notes about where to plug the CMS later (which files to replace).- Keep code neat, well-commented, and idiomatic TypeScript/React.Important constraints (do not implement)- Do not build the CMS, user authentication, or live edit features now. Only create the static visuals and seed data.- Do not include external analytics or tracking scripts.- Do not use non-free or proprietary fonts; prefer Google Fonts or system fallbacks.Tone for copywriting- Confident, concise, and human. Provide short placeholder copy for name, tagline, project descriptions, and experience bullets that reads like a senior engineer (you can use realistic but fictional content).Final note- Make the bento grids a signature element — they should be visually distinct, memorable, and adaptable so the future CMS can change tile sizes/content. Prioritize a pristine mobile experience, while delivering an elegant and airy desktop layout.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n_**Agent (model claude-4.5-opus-high-thinking, mode Agent)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"&lt;!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 --&gt;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"&lt;!-- cursor Session d136b2bd-7cc9-423b-94e6-d1e6f40e0054 (2025-12-01 10:48Z) --&gt;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# Static portfolio website design specifications (2025-12-01 10:48Z)\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":5},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":6},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"_**User (2025-12-01 08:24Z)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":7},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Interprets this prompt that I am gonna use for v0 @Browser and divide it in paragraphs:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":9},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":10},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":11},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":12},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Create a single, production-ready, static portfolio website (frontend only) for an elite software engineer. Always start from the top and only move to the next source if the current one doesn't have the answer.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Priority | Source | What it contains |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| 1 | &#96;AGENTS.md&#96; (this file) | Project-specific conventions, templates, and decisions |\\\\\\\\n| 2 | Sub &#96;AGENTS-*.md&#96; files | Deep-dive guidelines (security, performance, accessibility, animations, testing) |\\\\\\\\n| 3 | Agent Skills (&#96;.agents/skills/&#96;) | Framework and tool knowledge (Next.js, Drizzle, better-auth, shadcn, etc.) |\\\\\\\\n| 4 | Indexed Docs (Cursor) | Official documentation indexed locally in Cursor |\\\\\\\\n| 5 | MCP Servers | Live browsing and external tool integrations |\\\\\\\\n| 6 | Web Search | Last resort — only when none of the above have the answer |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Important**: Always prefer Cursor's indexed docs over web searches.                                               |\\\\\\\\n| Styling        | Tailwind CSS 4.1 with tw-animate-css                                       |\\\\\\\\n| Package Manager| pnpm v10.x They directly affect search rankings and represent the three pillars of page quality: loading, interactivity, and visual stability.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) — Loading\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nMeasures how long it takes for the largest visible element (hero image, heading, or main content block) to render.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Rating | Threshold |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Good | ≤ 2.5 seconds |\\\\\\\\n| Needs Improvement | 2.5s – 4.0s |\\\\\\\\n| Poor | &gt; 4.0 seconds |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**What optimizes LCP in this project:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Use &#96;priority&#96; prop on above-the-fold images (&#96;next/image&#96;) — skips lazy loading, preloads the image\\\\\\\\n- Use &#96;next/font&#96; for font loading — eliminates render-blocking external font requests\\\\\\\\n- Minimize server response time — keep Turso queries fast, use &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; with &#96;cacheLife&#96; for data that doesn't change every request\\\\\\\\n- Avoid large client-side JavaScript on the public page — keep it as a Server Component\\\\\\\\n- Use &#96;loading.tsx&#96; files — the static shell renders immediately while data streams in\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### INP (Interaction to Next Paint) — Interactivity\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nMeasures the latency of all user interactions (clicks, taps, key presses) throughout the page lifecycle. 12|\\\\\\\\n    13|Create a single, production-ready, static portfolio website (frontend only) for an elite software engineer. Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast &gt;= AA.Technical constraints &amp; stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout &amp; sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta &amp; SEO   - Proper &#96;&lt;head&gt;&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact &amp; social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system &amp; visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing &amp; grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance &amp; best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). Focus on mobile-first but ensure excellent desktop layouts. Use Next.js 16 (app router) + TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 and shadcn/ui for components. Do not implement any CMS, backend, or dynamic data sources — produce a static site with clearly labeled placeholder data files (JSON or TS) that will later be wired to a custom CMS. The public site must remain fully static for now.Design goals- Tone: Minimalist, modern aesthetic, clear, and highly scannable.- Special layout element: include multiple bento grids in the visual design (at least two distinct bento-style grids — e.g., Projects and Work Highlights or Projects and Side Projects/Case Studies). Bento grids should feel modular and crafted (tiles of mixed aspect ratios, consistent gutters, intentional negative space).- Emphasize whitespace, strong typographic hierarchy, and modest micro-animations (fade/scale/slide) only where they add clarity.- Accessibility: semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, ARIA for complex widgets, and WCAG color contrast &gt;= AA.Technical constraints &amp; stack specifics- Next.js 16 using the app/ directory and server components where appropriate. Use TypeScript everywhere.- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first); include a small global CSS file (e.g., &#96;styles/globals.css&#96;) that &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; and declares your &#96;@theme&#96; tokens. If needed, include a short note showing where to load a legacy &#96;tailwind.config.js&#96; via &#96;@config&#96;.- UI primitives: shadcn/ui components (Avatar, Card, Button, Tabs, Badge, Toast/ToastProvider, Dialog for contact modal, etc.). Use those for consistent styling.- Images: use &#96;next/image&#96; for optimization. Provide a circular/rounded slot for a face photo with an accessible &#96;alt&#96; and a fallback SVG.- Project data / experiences / employment mode: create a &#96;data/&#96; or &#96;lib/seed.ts&#96; file with typed placeholders (array of projects, experiences, boolean &#96;isEmployed&#96;) — do not implement toggling logic; just include the static value and render UI accordingly.- File structure: produce a clean, modular structure (&#96;app/&#96;, &#96;components/&#96;, &#96;lib/&#96; or &#96;data/&#96;, &#96;styles/&#96;, &#96;public/&#96;).- Types: supply clear TypeScript interfaces for Project, Experience, SocialLink, etc.Layout &amp; sections (mobile-first)1. Top meta &amp; SEO   - Proper &#96;&lt;head&gt;&#96; metadata: title, description, og:image placeholder, twitter card.2. Hero (above the fold)   - Small circular face photo slot (prominent but balanced).   - Name (H1), Role (H2), 1–2 line punchy tagline/bio.   - Primary CTAs: “View projects” (scroll to Projects) and “Download resume” (link to static PDF in /public).   - A compact status indicator near the name: &#96;Employed&#96; / &#96;Open to work&#96; (rendered from the static boolean).3. Key skills strip   - Horizontal, scrollable chips on mobile; grouped badges on desktop.4. Bento Grid — Projects   - A responsive, masonry-like bento grid of project cards (mixed tile sizes: 1x1, 2x1, 1x2).   - Each tile: project image, short title, 1-line tagline, tech badges on hover, and a subtle CTA “Case study” / “Repo”.   - On mobile show 2 columns; tablet 3; desktop 4–6 depending on width. Maintain consistent gutter (16px/1rem).5. Bento Grid — Work Highlights / Case Studies   - Second distinct bento grid used to highlight 3–6 big wins or case studies with larger hero tiles and short metrics.6. About / Bio   - Short narrative, timeline style mini-education or who-I-am box. Include a “Download CV” and a subtle photo repeat.7. Experience (static)   - Chronological cards — company, role, dates, 2–3 bullets. Keep compact for mobile; detail on desktop.8. Mini demo / code sample   - A small stylized code card (use JetBrains Mono or system-mono) showing a 6–10 line code snippet and a button to view repo.9. Contact &amp; social   - Email contact CTA, social icons (GitHub, LinkedIn, X, Mastodon if desired). Include a modal contact form (static — no backend).10. Footer    - Copyright, small nav, link to resume and privacy.Design system &amp; visual details- Colors: minimal neutral palette + one accent.  - Example palette (use these hex suggestions but feel free to adapt minimally): Background &#96;#0F1724&#96; or off-white &#96;#F8FAFC&#96; (light/dark support), Surface &#96;#FFFFFF&#96;/&#96;#0B1220&#96;, Accent &#96;#6C5CE7&#96; or &#96;#7C3AED&#96;, Muted text &#96;#64748B&#96;.  - Provide both light and dark themes toggle (persisted to localStorage) but default to system preference.- Typography:  - Sans variable for UI (Inter or Inter var) and monospace for code (JetBrains Mono).  - Large, readable sizes: mobile H1 ≈ 28–32px, desktop H1 ≈ 44–56px.- Spacing &amp; grid:  - Mobile-first spacing scale, consistent container widths and max-width for desktop (e.g., &#96;max-w-6xl&#96;).  - Bento tile sizing semantics: define utility classes or a &#96;tile&#96; component that accepts &#96;cols&#96; and &#96;rows&#96;.- Components:  - Reusable &#96;Avatar&#96;, &#96;ClippedImage&#96;, &#96;BentoGrid&#96; (configurable), &#96;ProjectCard&#96;, &#96;ExperienceCard&#96;, &#96;SkillChips&#96;, &#96;Navbar&#96; (minimal), &#96;Footer&#96;.  - &#96;BentoGrid&#96; should accept tile definitions so a future CMS can drive layout.- Micro-interactions:  - Subtle hover elevation (translateY -4px, shadow) and focus rings for accessibility. Use &#96;prefers-reduced-motion&#96;.- Performance &amp; best practices:  - Optimize images, use lazy loading, prefetch critical resources, static rendering (no client-only heavy JS).  - Semantic HTML and ARIA attributes for interactive components.IMPORTANT TAILWIND v4 NOTES (follow these rules)- Use Tailwind CSS v4 (CSS-first). Import Tailwind in your CSS with &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96;, not &#96;@tailwind&#96; directives.- Define design tokens, custom utilities, and settings in CSS using the new &#96;@theme&#96; at-rule and related directives (so there is no default &#96;tailwind.config.ts&#96;). If you intentionally want to keep a legacy JS/TS configuration, load it explicitly from CSS using &#96;@config \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"./tailwind.config.js\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; (this is allowed for backward compatibility), but prefer CSS-first. - Use &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; for PostCSS setups or &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; when using Vite/Next dev tooling. Use &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; for CLI commands. - Keep compatibility with Tailwind v4 features: automatic content detection, CSS theme variables, container queries, and prefers-reduced-motion handling.Deliverables (explicit)- Output a complete project scaffold (files and code) ready to run with &#96;pnpm&#96;/&#96;npm&#96;:  - &#96;app/page.tsx&#96; (home)  - &#96;app/layout.tsx&#96; (meta, fonts, theme provider)  - &#96;components/*&#96; for each UI piece  - &#96;lib/data.ts&#96; or &#96;data/seed.ts&#96; with typed placeholder data  - &#96;public/&#96; with placeholder images (profile SVG) and &#96;resume.pdf&#96;  - &#96;styles/globals.css&#96; containing &#96;@import \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"tailwindcss\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\";&#96; and your &#96;@theme&#96; declarations  - &#96;postcss.config.mjs&#96; referencing &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; if using PostCSS, or instructions to use &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; for Vite users  - &#96;package.json&#96; with &#96;tailwindcss&#96; v4 and &#96;@tailwindcss/postcss&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/vite&#96; / &#96;@tailwindcss/cli&#96; as appropriate- Include a small README with run instructions and notes about where to plug the CMS later (which files to replace).- Keep code neat, well-commented, and idiomatic TypeScript/React.Important constraints (do not implement)- Do not build the CMS, user authentication, or live edit features now. Only create the static visuals and seed data.- Do not include external analytics or tracking scripts.- Do not use non-free or proprietary fonts; prefer Google Fonts or system fallbacks.Tone for copywriting- Confident, concise, and human. Provide short placeholder copy for name, tagline, project descriptions, and experience bullets that reads like a senior engineer (you can use realistic but fictional content).Final note- Make the bento grids a signature element — they should be visually distinct, memorable, and adaptable so the future CMS can change tile sizes/content. Prioritize a pristine mobile experience, while delivering an elegant and airy desktop layout.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n_**Agent (model claude-4.5-opus-high-thinking, mode Agent)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"&lt;!-- Generated by SpecStory, Markdown v2.1.0 --&gt;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":1},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":2},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"&lt;!-- cursor Session d136b2bd-7cc9-423b-94e6-d1e6f40e0054 (2025-12-01 10:48Z) --&gt;\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":3},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":4},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"# Static portfolio website design specifications (2025-12-01 10:48Z)\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":5},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":6},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"_**User (2025-12-01 08:24Z)**_\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":7},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":8},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Interprets this prompt that I am gonna use for v0 @Browser and divide it in paragraphs:\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":9},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":10},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":11},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":12},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Create a single, production-ready, static portfolio website (frontend only) for an elite software engineer. SEO-optimized |\\\\\\\\n| Skills multi-select | Client | Combobox interactivity (cmdk) |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## Core Web Vitals\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nCore Web Vitals are the three metrics Google uses to measure real-world user experience. They directly affect search rankings and represent the three pillars of page quality: loading, interactivity, and visual stability.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) — Loading\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nMeasures how long it takes for the largest visible element (hero image, heading, or main content block) to render.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Rating | Threshold |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Good | ≤ 2.5 seconds |\\\\\\\\n| Needs Improvement | 2.5s – 4.0s |\\\\\\\\n| Poor | &gt; 4.0 seconds |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**What optimizes LCP in this project:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Use &#96;priority&#96; prop on above-the-fold images (&#96;next/image&#96;) — skips lazy loading, preloads the image\\\\\\\\n- Use &#96;next/font&#96; for font loading — eliminates render-blocking external font requests\\\\\\\\n- Minimize server response time — keep Turso queries fast, use &#96;\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"use cache\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"&#96; with &#96;cacheLife&#96; for data that doesn't change every request\\\\\\\\n- Avoid large client-side JavaScript on the public page — keep it as a Server Component\\\\\\\\n- Use &#96;loading.tsx&#96; files — the static shell renders immediately while data streams in\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### INP (Interaction to Next Paint) — Interactivity\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nMeasures the latency of all user interactions (clicks, taps, key presses) throughout the page lifecycle. The worst interaction (at the 98th percentile) becomes the INP score.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n| Rating | Threshold |\\\\\\\\n| --- | --- |\\\\\\\\n| Good | ≤ 200 milliseconds |\\\\\\\\n| Needs Improvement | 200ms – 500ms |\\\\\\\\n| Poor | &gt; 500 milliseconds |\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**What optimizes INP in this project:**\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- React Compiler auto-memoizes components — fewer unnecessary re-renders on interaction\\\\\\\\n- Server Components by default — minimal client-side JavaScript means fewer things competing for the main thread\\\\\\\\n- Dynamic imports for heavy components — keeps the initial JS bundle small\\\\\\\\n- Avoid heavy synchronous work in event handlers — defer to &#96;startTransition&#96; or Server Actions for mutations\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"signatures\\\\\\\":{},\\\\\\\"detailedLines\\\\\\\":[{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| Delete confirmation dialog | Client | Modal state, click handlers |\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":315},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| Login form | Client | Form state, submission handling |\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":316},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| Public portfolio page | Server | Static rendering, SEO-optimized |\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":317},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"| Skills multi-select | Client | Combobox interactivity (cmdk) |\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":318},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":319},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"---\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":320},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":321},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"## Core Web Vitals\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":322},{\\\\\\\"lineNumber\\\\\\\":323},{\\\\\\\"text\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"Core Web Vitals are the three metrics Google uses to measure real-world user experience.
